market_holds: Spot $334.19 at the 2026-11-19 close (sealed baseline). It is down 2.2% over 20 sessions and 25% below the $448.85 52-week high of 2026-08-17. Most of the fall since August tracks the A&D sector (ITA -17.9% from Aug 14 to Oct 19 on a Democratic-sweep budget scare, and defense names fell again on Nov 4 after the midterms), so it is not a Moog-specific de-rating. The option chain is unusable for an event read: 515 total open interest, an ATM spread of 24% of mid, and an event-implied move that backs out to 0.0%. The usual move is a 6.02% median absolute over 7 prints (+6.0, +8.2, +2.3 and -7.0 over the last four). Q4 FY26 consensus is EPS $2.70 on $1.12bn (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-15). The company's FY26 guide of $11.65 +/- 0.10, less Q1-Q3 adjusted EPS of 2.63 + 2.64 + 3.72 = 8.99, implies about $2.66 for Q4, so consensus sits on the guide. FY27 EPS consensus is about $12.14-12.24 (Fox/LSEG 12.14 with a range of 11.64-12.81, as of 2026-11-19; StockAnalysis/Yahoo 12.24 on $4.73bn revenue) and was revised up about 10% over three months, so it is not stale. FY26 adjusted EPS includes a roughly $30m IEEPA tariff refund in operating profit (about $0.70 a share by the preview's count). The print will trade on the first FY27 guide against that bar, and on whether the FY26 base is cleaned of the refund.
view: This is a guide print. The quarter will probably beat: Moog beat its own implied quarter by $0.30-0.40 in each of Q1, Q2 and Q3, so Q4 near $2.9-3.0 against $2.70 is likely. The beat will not decide the reaction, though; the initial FY27 guide will. The base for FY27 is FY26 without the tariff refund, roughly $11.2-11.3. Last year's initial guide was +15% over FY25 actual and came in above FactSet ($10.00 against $9.64), and the stock rose 8.2%. The year before, the guide was $8.20 against $8.26, slightly below. The same posture now (sales +6-8%, 50-80bp of margin) gives roughly $12.3-12.8. That is at or a little above a consensus of about $12.2 that has already been revised up. Against that: TransDigm's FY27 guide (+15% EPS) still missed the whisper and the stock fell about 4% on 2026-11-10, Curtiss-Wright's beat-and-raise got a muted-to-negative response, and a Democratic Congress makes a cautious defense line in the guide plausible (missiles, MV75 timing, a continuing resolution). Positioning is lighter than in July, after a 25% drawdown and a sector de-rating, so a clean guide has room to work, but the sector tape is a headwind. The net lean is mildly up, not far enough from a coin flip to bet on.

recommendation.reason: The decisive line is the initial FY27 EPS guide against a consensus of about $12.2. That consensus was revised up recently, so it is not stale. My own rebuild of Moog's conservative-but-growing guide style lands at or slightly above it, not clearly beyond it. The sector's recent reception of FY27 guides (TDG -4% on a +15% guide) shows the real bar is above the printed consensus. I can name no dated datapoint that the price does not hold, so there is no mechanism to bet on.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A FY27 adjusted EPS guide midpoint of $12.75 or more, with the tariff refund stripped out of the base, would make up likely. A guide at or below $12.0, or explicit caution on defense funding timing, would make down likely.

self_critique: The case for up is stronger than 55 suggests. Moog has beaten and raised four quarters running, is conservative by habit, and FY27 should carry less tariff pressure (FY26 absorbed about 110bp) on top of data-center cooling doubling and the missile ramp. The stock is near the post-earnings low end of its range after a sector de-rating, so a FY27 guide of $12.75 or more could move it +8%, as happened last November. The case for down: the refund-inflated FY26 base invites a 'guide below the run-rate' headline, a Democratic Congress gives management reason to be cautious on defense, and TDG shows the sector selling guides that only meet consensus. With both cases credible, I hold near 50.
approach_notes: P4 (prove 'priced in') helped: checking revision direction showed the FY27 consensus is fresh, which killed the stale-estimate angle. Peer reactions to FY27 guides (P3, stakeholders) were the most useful outside evidence. The illiquid option chain left no real implied move to anchor on, and the playbook gives no fallback beyond the historical median.
